newsitem.title: FRANCE: DEXIA BUYS 40 PERCENT OF ITALY'S CREDIOP.
newsitem.headline: DEXIA BUYS 40 PERCENT OF ITALY'S CREDIOP.

text.p: Franco-Belgian bank Dexia said on Monday it had agreed a long-term strategic cooperation pact with Italy's group San Paolo and would take a 40 percent stake in Italy's Crediop.
In a statement Dexia said the price would be between 1.6 and 1.9 billion French francs, the final price depending on the Crediop performance in the next three years.

Dexia, created in October out of the merger of Credit Local de France and Credit Communal de Belgique, said it planned to take a one percent stake in Institutio Bancario San Paolo di Torino during its privatisation later in 1997.
The operation will be financed by Dexia's own funds and will be positive for results and profitability from 1997, Dexia said in the statement.

"Already active in Great Britain, Germany, Spain, Austria and Sweden, Dexia could not be absent from one of the large European Union markets, Italy," chairman Pierre Richard said. "By this important operation, Dexia completes its European network."
Dexia said Crediop SpA has a balance sheet total of 110 billion francs and shareholders assets of 3.3 billion francs, making it the biggest local sector bank after Cassa Depositi e Presititi.
Crediop said on Monday it posted an 11-month profit of 71.5 billion lira. It has been under San Paolo ownership since February 1, 1996.
Dexia has a balance sheet total of over 1,000 billion francs and shareholders funds of 40 billion francs.
